placements.title: A signed release manifest becomes a precondition for shipping, not a review step
placements.frame: What must a release artifact carry before it reaches staging or production, and who holds the authority to require it?
placements.why: No existing leaves were supplied, so nothing is reusable. ReleaseGateRequirement holds the directive (src-1), the recorded gate rule (src-4), its staging and production scope (src-5), and the named owner (src-6). Together they state a standing requirement that a signed manifest gates Meridian deploys. This is a subject future envelopes will keep feeding (release provenance and deploy gating), not a single fact, so it passes the grain test. It stands alone as foundational because nothing exists to hold it under.

mints.name: ReleaseGateSigning
mints.title: Signed release manifests gating Meridian deploys to staging and production
mints.why: No existing strata were supplied. The gate and its signing requirement form a subject the organization returns to, so the theme groups the narrative and its position together.

mints.why: The content draws an explicit line from a cause (unsigned artifacts reached staging) to what it drove (the gate). This is a causal relationship, so it is minted as a causal stratum.

The position holds the gate requirement (thematic) and cites the unsigned staging incident as its cause (causal).
